messages:
maya: quick question — when a request is routed to a lower-tier fallback model because of quota or capacity, should the client see 429 or 503?
jun: hm, depends what we want clients to do. 429 implies 'you exceeded quota', 503 implies 'service temporarily unavailable'. both are accurate but different signals.
sam: leaning 429 if it's quota-driven, 503 if it's capacity/region failover. otherwise clients won't distinguish fallback vs hard limit.
elaine: agree, but we currently have many cases where we return 200 with a header X-Redwood-Fallback: true. that hides the fact that traffic was downgraded. ops/partners want clearer telemetry and customer hints.
alex: can we do both? 200 + header for transparent fallbacks (no client action), but emit a distinct status when fallback is due to quota enforcement so client can choose to back off.
maya: tricky for SDKs. they expect consistent status semantics. mixing 200/429/503 for similar outcomes may break retry logic.
jun: proposal: canonical error surface = {quota_exceeded => 429 + Retry-After, capacity_fallback => 200 + X-Redwood-Fallback=soft, capacity_block => 503}. also include X-Redwood-Route-Reason header values: "quota", "fallback", "region-err".
sam: +1. also add a small JSON body when non-200 with an actionable message: {"code":"quota_exceeded","hint":"reduce tokens or request higher tier","quota_type":"burst"}. keeps SDK parsing easy.
elaine: for console badges, we should surface a 'Degraded' badge when any fallback header appears, and a 'Throttled' badge specifically for 429s. telemetry events should include route_reason and model_variant.
maya: question for infra-bot: can current routing stack attach route_reason to logs and metrics?
infra-bot: routing stack update status: can propagate route_reason into request span and metrics via tag 'route.reason' since last deploy (168h). needs 2 small schema updates for log ingestion.
alex: rollout plan: feature-flag the headers + body, enable in staging for 48h, add SDK patch to expose X-Redwood-Route-Reason and parse structured body for non-200. then enable console badging in canary.
jun: also add a mapping table in docs: 429 -> client backoff, 503 -> retry later (idempotent contexts), 200+fallback -> no client change but telemetry note. examples for retry semantics please.
sam: I'll draft the docs snippets and sample SDK code this afternoon.
elaine: I'll update the dashboard spec: add metric 'fallback_rate' per model_variant and 'throttle_rate' per tenant. wire up alert when fallback_rate > 5% and throttle_rate > 1%.
maya: action items: sam docs, alex feature flag, infra deploy schema updates, elaine dashboard patches. owners agree? :thumbsup:
jun: :thumbsup:
sam: :thumbsup: will ping when drafts ready.
alex: created feature-flag: ff/route-signal-enhanced (internal). turning on in staging now.
infra-bot: deploy triggered for routing-service v3.2.1 -> staging.
maya: thanks all — good to get consistent signals across API, SDK, and console.
